BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

1	package search
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"net/http"
10		"net/url"
11		"strconv"
12		"strings"
13		"time"
14	
15		ulid "github.com/oklog/ulid/v2"
16	
17		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/api"
18	)
19	
20	const apiTimeout = 30 * time.Second
21	
22	// v4ServicePath is the per-repo v4 query-serve route exposed by the entire-api
23	// cell gateway. It takes repo=<ULID>. The BFF (entire.io /api/v1/search)
24	// forwards to this same path; the CLI dials the cell directly with a
25	// jurisdictional identity token, skipping the BFF hop.
26	const v4ServicePath = "/api/v1/semantic-search/search/v1/search"
27	
28	// ErrCellUnavailable reports that a cell's gateway does not expose the
29	// semantic-search route at all (HTTP 404 at the route level) — query-serve is
30	// not deployed in that cell yet. Callers fanning out across cells match it
31	// with errors.Is and skip the cell quietly instead of warning the user about
32	// a "failed" region.
33	var ErrCellUnavailable = errors.New("semantic search is not available in this cell")
34	
35	// WildcardQuery is the query string used when only filters are provided (no search terms).
36	const WildcardQuery = "*"
37	
38	// AllReposFilter is the inline repo filter value that disables repo scoping.
39	const AllReposFilter = "*"
40	
41	// Result type constants.
42	const (
43		TypeCheckpoint = "checkpoint"
44		TypeCommit     = "commit"
45		TypeSession    = "session"
46		// TypeRepo and TypePR are returned by the backend but have no typed struct
47		// (decoded via rawData). They're named so the cross-cell v4 merge can bucket
48		// and tally them without string literals.
49		TypeRepo = "repo"
50		TypePR   = "pr"
51	)
52	
53	// DefaultLimit is the default number of results to fetch per request, matching the UI.
54	const DefaultLimit = 100
55	
56	// Meta contains search ranking metadata for a result.
57	type Meta struct {
58		MatchType string   `json:"matchType"`
59		Score     float64  `json:"score"`
60		Tier      *int     `json:"tier,omitempty"`
61		Snippet   string   `json:"snippet,omitempty"`
62		Summary   string   `json:"summary,omitempty"`
63		BM25Score *float64 `json:"bm25Score,omitempty"`
64		ANNScore  *float64 `json:"annScore,omitempty"`
65	}
66	
67	// CheckpointResult represents a checkpoint returned by the search service.
68	type CheckpointResult struct {
69		ID             string   `json:"id"`
70		Prompt         string   `json:"prompt"`
71		CommitMessage  *string  `json:"commitMessage"`
72		CommitSubject  *string  `json:"commitSubject"`
73		CommitSHA      *string  `json:"commitSha"`
74		Branch         string   `json:"branch"`
75		Org            string   `json:"org"`
76		Repo           string   `json:"repo"`
77		Author         string   `json:"author"`
78		AuthorUsername *string  `json:"authorUsername"`
79		CreatedAt      string   `json:"createdAt"`
80		FilesTouched   []string `json:"filesTouched"`
81	}
82	
83	// CommitResult represents a commit returned by the search service.
84	type CommitResult struct {
85		ID             string  `json:"id"`
86		CommitSHA      string  `json:"commitSha"`
87		CommitMessage  string  `json:"commitMessage"`
88		CommitSubject  string  `json:"commitSubject"`
89		Branch         string  `json:"branch"`
90		Org            string  `json:"org"`
91		Repo           string  `json:"repo"`
92		Author         string  `json:"author"`
93		AuthorUsername *string `json:"authorUsername"`
94		CreatedAt      string  `json:"createdAt"`
95		Additions      int     `json:"additions"`
96		Deletions      int     `json:"deletions"`
97		FilesChanged   int     `json:"filesChanged"`
98		HTMLUrl        *string `json:"htmlUrl"`
99	}
100	
101	// SessionResult represents a session returned by the search service.
102	type SessionResult struct {
103		SessionID      string  `json:"sessionId"`
104		DisplayName    string  `json:"displayName"`
105		Prompt         *string `json:"prompt"`
106		Agent          *string `json:"agent"`
107		Model          *string `json:"model"`
108		StepCount      int     `json:"stepCount"`
109		Org            string  `json:"org"`
110		Repo           string  `json:"repo"`
111		Branch         *string `json:"branch"`
112		AuthorUsername *string `json:"authorUsername"`
113		CreatedAt      string  `json:"createdAt"`
114	}
115	
116	// Result wraps a search result with its type and ranking metadata.
117	// Exactly one of Checkpoint, Commit, or Session is non-nil based on Type.
118	type Result struct {
119		Type       string            `json:"-"`
120		Meta       Meta              `json:"-"`
121		Checkpoint *CheckpointResult `json:"-"`
122		Commit     *CommitResult     `json:"-"`
123		Session    *SessionResult    `json:"-"`
124	
125		// rawData preserves the original JSON for unknown types (repo, pr).
126		rawData json.RawMessage
127		// rawFields is rawData decoded once at unmarshal time, and only for types
128		// without a typed struct (repo, pr) — accessors never read raw fields for
129		// typed rows, so a backend field addition cannot change what they return.
130		rawFields map[string]json.RawMessage
131	}
132	
133	// resultJSON is the wire format for JSON marshaling/unmarshaling.
134	type resultJSON struct {
135		Type string          `json:"type"`
136		Data json.RawMessage `json:"data"`
137		Meta Meta            `json:"searchMeta"`
138	}
139	
140	// MarshalJSON implements custom JSON marshaling to produce the API wire format.
141	func (r *Result) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
142		var data any
143		switch r.Type {
144		case TypeCheckpoint:
145			data = r.Checkpoint
146		case TypeCommit:
147			data = r.Commit
148		case TypeSession:
149			data = r.Session
150		default:
151			data = r.rawData
152		}
153		raw, err := json.Marshal(data)
154		if err != nil {
155			return nil, fmt.Errorf("marshaling result data: %w", err)
156		}
157		out, err := json.Marshal(resultJSON{
158			Type: r.Type,
159			Data: raw,
160			Meta: r.Meta,
161		})
162		if err != nil {
163			return nil, fmt.Errorf("marshaling result: %w", err)
164		}
165		return out, nil
166	}
167	
168	// UnmarshalJSON implements custom JSON unmarshaling to parse typed data.
169	func (r *Result) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {
170		var raw resultJSON
171		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
172			return fmt.Errorf("unmarshaling result: %w", err)
173		}
174		r.Type = raw.Type
175		r.Meta = raw.Meta
176		r.rawData = raw.Data
177		// Clear any previously-decoded payloads so a reused Result keeps the
178		// "exactly one typed pointer is non-nil" invariant.
179		r.Checkpoint, r.Commit, r.Session = nil, nil, nil
180		r.rawFields = nil
181	
182		switch raw.Type {
183		case TypeCheckpoint:
184			var d CheckpointResult
185			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw.Data, &d); err != nil {
186				return fmt.Errorf("unmarshaling checkpoint data: %w", err)
187			}
188			r.Checkpoint = &d
189		case TypeCommit:
190			var d CommitResult
191			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw.Data, &d); err != nil {
192				return fmt.Errorf("unmarshaling commit data: %w", err)
193			}
194			r.Commit = &d
195		case TypeSession:
196			var d SessionResult
197			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw.Data, &d); err != nil {
198				return fmt.Errorf("unmarshaling session data: %w", err)
199			}
200			r.Session = &d
201		default:
202			// Unknown types (repo, pr): decode the payload once so accessors can
203			// read identifying fields without re-parsing per call (the TUI calls
204			// them per row per render).
205			_ = json.Unmarshal(raw.Data, &r.rawFields) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort; accessors return "" when nil
206		}
207		return nil
208	}
209
